overall_summary: First-person immersive exoplanet exploration and 'What If You Fell Into...' extreme environment survival scenarios heavily dominate channel viewership and engagement (800-1,000+ views, 3-4% like-to-view ratios). In contrast, generic psychology facts, repeated identical trivia uploads, and abstract space sound/memory facts systematically stagnate below 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-person visceral survival scenarios on extreme celestial bodies ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (974 views, 18 likes) yield the highest raw traffic and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Adopt cinematic first-person hypothetical journey hooks exploring extreme physics and hostile environments.

winning_patterns.pattern: High-contrast paradox titles highlighting extreme planetary conditions
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,032 views, 36 likes) and 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' (1,057 views, 8 likes) outperformed typical fact shorts by 5x-10x.
winning_patterns.action: Lead with tangible sensory paradoxes (e.g., metallic oceans, crushing magnetic fields, solid gas).

weak_patterns.pattern: Repetitive generic brain and psychology trivia
weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5, 10, 53 views) and 'Songs Stuck in Your Head' (17, 71 views) consistently failed to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Retire worn-out psychology listicle topics and focus on visceral, high-stakes curiosity.

weak_patterns.pattern: Re-uploading duplicate topics without substantive visual or narrative elevation
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' repeated three times achieved only 34 to 220 views with minimal interaction.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict uniqueness rules; explore novel astronomical and environmental phenomena instead of looping staples.

next_video.hook_style: First-person sensory jeopardy ('What if you fell into...')
next_video.concept: What would actually happen to a human body falling through Jupiter's supercritical metallic hydrogen ocean.
next_video.opening_direction: Instant plunge: show a spacesuit plummeting past swirling ammonia stormclouds straight into pitch-black crushing atmospheric pressure.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the gas does not hit a solid surface; instead, pressure forces hydrogen to liquefy into an ocean of glowing liquid metal where gravity tears atoms apart.
next_video.reason: Leverages the channel's proven high-performing 'What If You Fell Into...' framing while introducing an iconic Solar System mystery that FACTVERSE has not yet covered.
